goal: Review a web application for routes, sessions, security headers, input and output encoding, and dependencies.
use: Review a web application for routes, sessions, security headers, input and output encoding, and dependencies. Use when asked to review a web app before release.

steps.note: Read the app setup. Open the entry points, the router or route table, the session and cookie configuration, and the build and dependency files.
Check routes. List every route and its method.
Check sessions and cookies. Cookies need `Secure`, `HttpOnly` and a `SameSite` value.
Check input and output. Flag untrusted data written into HTML, JavaScript, URLs or SQL without encoding or parameters.
Check headers. Look for Content-Security-Policy, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options and a Referrer-Policy.
Check dependencies. Note packages with known advisories and scripts that run at install time.

protocol.title: Read the app setup
protocol.text: Open the entry points, the router or route table, the session and cookie configuration, and the build and dependency files.

protocol.title: Check routes
protocol.text: List every route and its method. Flag routes that change state with GET, and admin routes that are reachable without a check.

protocol.title: Check sessions and cookies
protocol.text: Cookies need `Secure`, `HttpOnly` and a `SameSite` value. Flag session IDs in URLs, and sessions that never expire.

protocol.title: Check input and output
protocol.text: Flag untrusted data written into HTML, JavaScript, URLs or SQL without encoding or parameters.

protocol.title: Check headers
protocol.text: Look for Content-Security-Policy, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options and a Referrer-Policy. Flag missing headers and `unsafe-inline` scripts.

protocol.title: Check dependencies
protocol.text: Note packages with known advisories and scripts that run at install time.

protocol.title: Check errors and logs
protocol.text: Flag stack traces shown to users, and secrets or personal data written to logs.

protocol.title: Report
protocol.text: List each finding as `file:line`, with severity (high, medium or low), the problem and the fix. Mark what you did not run.
